calls.head: There’s no curse: Luukkonen vs. The Maple Leafs
calls.body: Luukkonen has been shaky against the Maple Leafs since 2023-24, well below his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if he looks like himself tonight.
calls.call: If Luukkonen starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .902 than to his .851 against the Maple Leafs.

calls.title: Luukkonen struggled against the Maple Leafs again
calls.plain: Luukkonen’s night looked more like his record against the Maple Leafs than his usual. Three seasons of evidence say it’s still a coincidence.
calls.said: Luukkonen’s rough record against the Maple Leafs was a coincidence, and he’d look like himself

calls.head: The Sabres should tilt the ice
calls.body: The Sabres have been near the top of the league at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Maple Leafs one of the worst. Expect the Sabres to spend more of the night in the Maple Leafs’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Gilbert sparks a Sabres comeback
paras: Two kinds of hat tricks in Toronto: the Maple Leafs’ Kirill Marchenko scored three goals, and the Sabres’ Jack Quinn got the Gordie Howe, a goal, an assist and a fight. Auston Matthews struck first for the Maple Leafs early in the first, but Quinn made it 1-1 for Buffalo a little over a minute later. Marchenko put the Maple Leafs back ahead 2-1 on the power play midway through the period. Quinn struck again early in the second to tie it 2-2. The Leafs’ Gavin McKenna didn’t play after 10:20 of the second period. Marchenko scored again midway through the period to put the Maple Leafs back ahead 3-2, and Quinn and Troy Stecher dropped the gloves late in the period. Marchenko completed his hat trick later in the period to make it 4-2 for the Maple Leafs. The Maple Leafs’ John Tavares left early in the third period and didn’t return. Two days later, he was listed as week to week with a lower-body injury. Dennis Gilbert and Mattias Samuelsson scored a little over two minutes apart midway through the period to tie it 4-4. Owen Power won it in overtime. Quinn added two assists for a four-point night.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen made 26 saves for the Sabres, and Sergei Bobrovsky allowed five goals on 34 shots. The Sabres improved to 4-3-1 and took fifth place in the Atlantic from the Maple Leafs, who fell to 3-3-2.

items.text: Auston Matthews extended his point streak against Buffalo to eleven games.
Auston Matthews has a point in six straight games, with a goal in each of the last three.
It was the Sabres’ first road win of the season, in their third road game.
The Sabres won without Rasmus Dahlin, Conor Timmins, Alex Lyon and others. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Wild were missing more at the time.
